R301.note: Whitelist on table name before interpolation correctly closes injection; illustrative whitelist disclosed as needing maintenance.

R302.note: exec.Command with separate args removes the shell entirely; functionally equivalent to original.

R303.note: setSecure(true) is the correct one-line fix, no other change.

R304.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet uses RESP length-prefixed framing, closing CRLF injection; DI signature change is stated plainly.

R305.note: mathjs.evaluate replaces Function constructor; scoped context correctly exposes order fields, error handling matches intent.

R306.note: resolve_entities=False plus no_network/load_dtd hardening is the standard XXE fix; no legitimate entity use broken.

R307.note: ORDER BY whitelist correctly closes injection; default 'created_at' from the controller is included in the whitelist.

R308.note: loadProjectExport never returns ownerId, so exportPayload.ownerId is always undefined -- the check as written 403s every caller including legitimate owners, and this isn't noted; alternative fix cites a canUserAccessProject module that doesn't exist in the codebase.

R309.note: secure flag flipped to true, matches setcookie() argument position, no other change.

R310.note: Whitelist {first_name,last_name,email,phone} correctly blocks injection, but the controller's default field value is 'name', which is not in the whitelist -- every request that omits ?field= (the default path) now raises ValueError, silently breaking the endpoint's default legitimate use; not mentioned in the write-up.

R311.note: Escapes the standard RFC4515 LDAP filter metacharacters before interpolation; correct primary defence.

R312.note: crypto/rand.Read with 16 bytes replaces math/rand; token format changes but nothing else depends on its shape.

R313.note: vector<string> instead of vector<string_view> lets push_back's move-construction own the data; matches remember()/firstLetter() exactly as claimed.

R314.note: secrets.randbelow with the min/max remap is the correct CSPRNG substitution; range edge case behaves the same as before (raises on invalid range).

R315.note: .at() correctly bounds-checks; the switch from silent OOB write to a thrown exception is stated plainly and valid slots are unaffected.

R316.note: Python logging's %s substitution does not strip or escape newlines -- record.getMessage() still embeds the literal '\n' from username, producing an identical forged log line to the f-string version; the write-up's claim that %s 'does not interpret newlines... as log structure' is false, so the reported injection is not closed.

R317.note: JSON.parse replaces node-serialize's unsafe eval-based deserializer; try/catch preserves the no-cookie empty-profile behavior.

R318.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode() on both interpolated values correctly neutralizes the HTML context; no other observable change.

R319.note: Unix branch is properly fixed, but on Windows the target program is still cmd.exe /c -- ProcessBuilder's argument array is reconstructed into a single command line that cmd.exe re-parses itself, so shell metacharacters in data remain interpretable there despite the array form.

R320.note: JavaScriptStringEncode only escapes JS-string metacharacters (quotes/backslash/control chars), not '<' or '/'; a payload like q=</script><script>alert(1)</script> is untouched by the encoder and still terminates the original <script> block early, so the reported XSS remains exploitable via a different route than the quote-breakout the fix addresses.

R321.note: Ping class correctly eliminates the shell; but it silently changes behavior from a 4-probe cmd.exe ping with full statistics output to a single Ping.Send() with a custom-formatted line, while the write-up incorrectly claims the original return-value pattern is 'preserved.'

R322.note: SandboxedEnvironment is a real hardening step, but the write-up itself states it 'does not eliminate template injection' and workarounds may exist -- the primary fix does not fully close the reported CWE-94 vector by its own admission; only the secondary architectural (template-ID) option does.

R323.note: escapeHtml4 on the Referer-derived param closes the injection; dropping the format() call also removes an unrelated format-string quirk with no legitimate use depending on it.

R324.note: Standard React text rendering replaces dangerouslySetInnerHTML; trade-off against rich-HTML use is explicitly discussed and justified by the stated context.

R325.note: resize(count) makes indices 0..count-1 valid before the indexed writes; preserves function contract for count <= fields.size().

R326.note: th:text replaces th:utext, switching to Thymeleaf's default HTML-entity encoding; correct minimal fix.

R327.note: Whitelist mapping from command name to a fixed handler-function set closes function-name injection into call_user_func_array; illustrative handler names are clearly meant to be adapted to real handlers.

R328.note: Extension whitelist plus a randomly generated filename closes both the dangerous-extension and filename-control vectors; upload still succeeds for legitimate image types.

R329.note: sqlite3 '?' placeholder with a parameter tuple is the correct parameterized-query fix.

R330.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) is the idiomatic fix for the auto-unboxing NPE; return semantics unchanged for present keys.

R331.note: DOM construction with textContent/createTextNode neutralizes both author and body fields while preserving the original span+colon layout.

R332.note: Caching node->next before free() is the standard safe traversal-with-deletion pattern.

R333.note: Same pattern as the Case15 case: the Unix branch is fixed, but the Windows branch still shells out via cmd.exe /c, which re-parses the reconstructed command line regardless of the argument-array form.

R334.note: Generic client message plus server-side logging with exc_info is the correct CWE-209 fix; status code and success path unchanged.

R335.note: Changing offset from int to size_t removes the signed/unsigned mismatch at its source so the bounds check and the pointer arithmetic agree; disclosed as a signature change.

R336.note: .at() (or the explicit range check) correctly bounds-checks the write; behavior change to a thrown exception is explained.

R337.note: Protocol allowlist via new URL() correctly blocks javascript:/data: schemes while still permitting http/https/mailto, with attribute-escaping kept as defense in depth.

R338.note: Column and direction allowlists close the ORDER BY injection; both controller defaults (created_at, DESC) pass the whitelist so default legitimate use is unaffected.

R339.note: NULL check before strcmp is the correct, minimal fix; unset-env-var case now safely returns 0 instead of crashing.

R340.note: PreparedStatement/setString is the right parameterization pattern, but OWASP Benchmark's DatabaseHelper exposes getSqlConnection(), not the getConnection() the fix calls -- as written this likely fails to compile against the real helper class.
